first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both declining, and prior evidence indicates onboarding simplification improves completion, time-to-value, and early adoption. This directly addresses the two observed internal funnel regressions while avoiding potentially less durable price-led acquisition. Verify the most relevant onboarding result and the pricing alternative before commitment because competitor pricing increases the opportunity cost of not responding commercially.

mid.rationale: Run a standard experiment simplifying onboarding. The verified prior result directly addresses both current declines: onboarding completion increased 13%, time-to-value fell 2.1 days, and 30-day retention rose 3%. This is aligned with sustainable qualified revenue, whereas verified promotional pricing produced a 12% 30-day retention decline despite short-term qualified-revenue growth.

final2.rationale: Maintain the onboarding-simplification experiment. The deeper competitor cut and doubled price-related churn raise urgency, but the available pricing evidence shows targeted 40% discounts caused a 12% 30-day retention decline and explicitly cautions against treating discounting as sustainable growth. There is no verified evidence that a new discount would prevent incumbent churn. Simplification directly addresses the concurrent 4% onboarding-completion and 6% activation declines, with verified prior gains in completion (+13%), time-to-value (-2.1 days), and 30-day retention (+3%). The risk flag reflects untested downside from not making an immediate price response in the affected SMB segment.
